summary.text: A 15-year-old male was found to have elevated fasting blood glucose at a routine physical examination in July 2020, without overt symptoms. In September 2021 he presented after a right forearm fracture and ultrasonography revealed hepatic steatosis. Metformin, later with biphasic insulin, did not achieve glycemic control, and a March 2024 adjustment produced no significant improvement after six weeks.

Immediately before Mazdutide, evaluation showed HbA1c 9.60%, serum uric acid 511 μmol/L, total cholesterol 6.08 mmol/L, triglycerides 1.84 mmol/L, BMI 30.64 kg/m², blood pressure 138/83 mmHg and hepatic steatosis on ultrasonography. Examination found supracollarbone fat pads, buffalo hump and acanthosis nigricans, with congenital amblyopia and diabetes in both parents and maternal grandparents. Diagnoses were T2DM, obesity, hyperuricemia and MASLD with hyperlipidemia.

Mazdutide was given subcutaneously once weekly at 2 mg for weeks 1 - 4, 4 mg for weeks 5 - 8 and 6 mg for weeks 9 - 12, maintained at 6 mg through week 36, then discontinued for the observation period of weeks 37 - 42. Insulin 12 IU nightly and oral metformin were given alongside, with controlled diet and aerobic exercise, weekly remote monitoring and scheduled in-person evaluations.

Per Table 2, BMI fell from 30.64 to 24.85 kg/m², HbA1c from 9.60% to 7.5%, serum uric acid from 511 to 322 μmol/L and triglycerides from 1.84 to 0.57 mmol/L at week 42. Ultrasonography at 14 weeks showed resolved hepatic steatosis. No adverse events, hypoglycemia or hypotension were reported, and benefits were sustained after treatment.
